\chapter{Chapter06 — Matrix Product Verification}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter06.LearningAndTesting.MatrixProductVerification}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product verification predicate]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $A$, $B$, and $C$ be $n\times n$ matrices over the field with two elements, and let
$x$ be a vector in the $n$-dimensional vector space over that field. The matrix product
verification predicate holds at $x$ exactly when $Cx=A(Bx)$ coordinatewise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product verification decision]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $A$, $B$, and $C$ be $n\times n$ matrices over the field with two elements, and let
$x$ be an $n$-dimensional vector over that field. The decision is true exactly when
$Cx=A(Bx)$ coordinatewise, and false otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product difference]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductDifference}
\label{FABL.matrixProductDifference}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
For natural $n$ and $n\times n$ matrices $A$, $B$, and $C'$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the
matrix product difference is $C'-AB$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Row of a matrix product difference]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductDifferenceRow}
\label{FABL.matrixProductDifferenceRow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductDifference, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$, $B$, and $C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over the
field with two elements, and let $i$ be a row index. The row of the matrix product
difference at index $i$ is the function on column indices $j$ whose value is the matrix
product difference of $A$, $B$, and $C'$ at $(i,j)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Matrix product verification criterion]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_iff_difference_mulVec_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_iff_difference_mulVec_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductDifference, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$,
and let $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The equalities $C'x=A(Bx)$ hold in every coordinate if and
only if $(C'-AB)x=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Verification decision criterion]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision_eq_true_iff}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision_eq_true_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductDifference, FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_iff_difference_mulVec_eq_zero, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, all $n\times n$ matrices $A,B,C'$ over the two-element
field, and every binary vector $x$ of length $n$, the verification decision accepts
exactly when $(C'-AB)x=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact products pass every verification]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_of_eq}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_of_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$,
and suppose $C'=AB$. Then for every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, one has $C'x=A(Bx)$ in every
coordinate.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonzero row of a matrix product difference]
\lean{FABL.exists_matrixProductDifferenceRow_ne_zero}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over the field with
two elements. If $C'\ne AB$, then at least one row of $C'-AB$ is nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dot product with a matrix difference row]
\lean{FABL.f₂DotProduct_matrixProductDifferenceRow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.matrixProductDifference, FABL.matrixProductDifferenceRow, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb F_2$,
let $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $x\in\mathbb F_2^n$. The dot product of row $i$ of
$C'-AB$ with $x$ equals the $i$th coordinate of $(C'-AB)x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Verified rows annihilate the test vector]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_imp_row_dot_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate_imp_row_dot_eq_zero}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$,
and let $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. If $C'x=A(Bx)$ in every coordinate, then for each row
index $i$, the dot product of row $i$ of $C'-AB$ with $x$ is zero in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero indicator from the binary sign]
\lean{FABL.f₂ZeroIndicator_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.binarySign, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
For every $b\in\mathbb F_2$, the indicator of $b=0$ equals $(1+\chi(b))/2$, where $\chi$
is the binary sign character.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product verification acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a probability density on the
$n$-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements, and let $A$, $B$, and $C$
be $n\times n$ matrices over that field. Define the acceptance probability as the
expectation under $\varphi$ of the indicator of the event $Cx=A(Bx)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Probability of a zero binary dot product]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductRowZeroProbability_eq}
\label{FABL.matrixProductRowZeroProbability_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expect_eq_one, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.f₂ZeroIndicator_eq, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_apply}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\phi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb F_2^n$ and let $\gamma\in\mathbb F_2^n$.
The $\phi$-expectation of the indicator that the binary dot product $\gamma\cdot x$ is
zero equals $\bigl(1+\mathbb E_{x\sim\phi}[(-1)^{\gamma\cdot x}]\bigr)/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Local work for matrix product verification]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, the local work assigned to matrix product verification is
$6n^2+4n+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on local verification work]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_le}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork}
\difficulty{2}
For every natural number $n$, the quantity $6n^2+4n+1$ is at most $11(n+1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic bound on local work]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_isBigO}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_isBigO}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_le}
\difficulty{3}
The verification's local work, as a function of the natural-number dimension $n$, is
asymptotically bounded by a constant multiple of $(n+1)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Cost of matrix product verification]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork}
For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the matrix product verification cost uses zero random
examples and zero membership queries, and its work is $r+6n^2+4n+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Additivity of verification work cost]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost_eq}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningCost.toTriple_injective, FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork}
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the cost with zero random-example calls, zero
queries, and $r$ units of work, added to the cost with zero calls, zero queries, and the
verification's local work at dimension $n$, equals the verification cost for parameters
$n$ and $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Seeded matrix product verification result]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and
let $s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a seed map. For a seed $b\in\{0,1\}^r$, define the
result to be the Boolean outcome of the matrix product verification decision on $A,B,C'$
and $s(b)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Seeded verification criterion]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult_eq_true_iff}
\label{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult_eq_true_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, let a
seed map each $r$-bit string to a vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, and fix an $r$-bit string.
The seeded test returns true exactly when $C'x=A(Bx)$ coordinatewise for the vector $x$
produced by that seed string.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Seeded matrix product verification program]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}

Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and
let $s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a seed map. The program draws the Boolean seed
vector used by the random-bit-vector program for parameters $n,r$, charges the specified
matrix-product verification local work for dimension $n$, and returns the seeded
verification result as a Boolean value; it uses membership-query access.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Seeded verification acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and
let $s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb{F}_2^n$ be a seed map. The seeded verification acceptance
probability is the expectation, over a uniformly random Boolean vector $b\in\{0,1\}^r$,
of $1$ when the seeded verification result is true and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Seeded verification probability]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_eq}
\label{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_uniformPushforward, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.uniformPushforward, FABL.matrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult_eq_true_iff, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and
let a seed map each $r$-bit string to a vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The probability, for
a uniformly random seed string, that $C'x=A(Bx)$ coordinatewise on the seeded vector
equals the acceptance probability under the density obtained by pushing the uniform seed
distribution forward through the seed map.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Perfect acceptance for correct products]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_eq_one_of_eq}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and
let a seed map each $r$-bit string to a vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$. If $C'=AB$, then the
seeded verification acceptance probability is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance bound for an incorrect product]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.uniformPushforward, FABL.matrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_le, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_eq, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$
matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$, and let a seed map each $r$-bit string to a vector in
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Suppose the density obtained by pushing the uniform seed distribution
forward has every nonzero Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$,
and suppose $C'\ne AB$. Then the seeded verification acceptance probability is at most
$(1+\varepsilon)/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product verification program]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationProgram}

Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. The
program is the seeded matrix product verification program using the canonical map from
Boolean vectors of length $n$ to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$; it uses membership-query access and
returns a Boolean value.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product verification bit count]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationRandomBits}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationRandomBits}
\leanok
For each natural number $n$, the matrix product verification random-bit count is $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Matrix product verification run distribution]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_matrixProductVerificationProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_matrixProductVerificationProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost, FABL.matrixProductVerificationProgram, FABL.matrixProductVerificationRandomBits, FABL.runWithCost_seededMatrixProductVerificationProgram, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{1}
For a natural number $n$, a Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, and matrices
$A,B,C\in\mathbb F_2^{n\times n}$, the verification program’s run law is that of a
uniformly random bit vector $b\in\{0,1\}^n$, paired with the decision whether $Cx=
A(Bx)$ for every coordinate, where $x$ is the vector in $\mathbb F_2^n$ corresponding to
$b$. The cost is $(0,0,n+6n^2+4n+1)$; it does not depend on $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Uniform verification acceptance probability]
\lean{FABL.uniformMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.uniformMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.𝔽₂}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. The
uniform matrix product verification acceptance probability is the expectation, for a
uniformly random $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, of $1$ when the matrix product verification
predicate on $A,B,C',x$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Seeded and uniform verification probabilities]
\lean{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_boolVector_eq}
\label{FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_boolVector_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.matrixProductVerificationPredicate, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult_eq_true_iff, FABL.uniformMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A,B,C'$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$. The acceptance probability for
the seeded test whose seed maps a uniformly random Boolean vector of length $n$
coordinatewise to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ equals the acceptance probability for the test on a
uniformly random $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, where each test accepts exactly when $C'x=A(Bx)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Unbiasedness of the uniform cube density]
\lean{FABL.uniformPushforward_id_isBiased_zero}
\label{FABL.uniformPushforward_id_isBiased_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.expectation_uniformPushforward, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.isBiased_iff_expectation, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.uniformPushforward, FABL.expect_vectorWalshCharacter}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the density on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ obtained by pushing
forward the uniform distribution on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ under the identity map has every
nonconstant Fourier coefficient equal to zero; equivalently, it is biased with bias $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Matrix verification algorithm specification]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductVerificationAlgorithm_spec}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007}
\label{FABL.matrixProductVerificationAlgorithm_spec}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.boolVectorF₂CubeEquiv, FABL.matrixProductDifference, FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost, FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision, FABL.matrixProductVerificationDecision_eq_true_iff, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_isBigO, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_le, FABL.matrixProductVerificationProgram, FABL.matrixProductVerificationRandomBits, FABL.runWithCost_matrixProductVerificationProgram, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.uniformMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.uniformMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_eq_one_of_eq, FABL.uniformMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability_le_half, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, and
three $n\times n$ matrices over the two-element field, the verification program's
output-and-cost law is the pushforward of a uniform Boolean string of length $n$ to the
acceptance result and the stated cost. Its decision accepts on input $x$ exactly when
$(C'-AB)x=0$, and it uses $n$ random bits. Its local work is at most $11(n+1)^2$ and is
asymptotically bounded by a constant multiple of $(n+1)^2$. If $C'=AB$, uniform-input
acceptance probability is one; if $C'\ne AB$, it is at most $1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Equivalence between Boolean strings and cube pairs]

For each natural number $\ell$, there is a bijection between Boolean strings of length
$2\ell$ and ordered pairs of binary vectors of length $\ell$, where entries are viewed
in the field with two elements.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product small-bias seed]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasSeed}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{

Let $n,a,b\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n>0$, $a>0$, and $2a\le b$, and let the requested bias
be encoded by $a/b$. For a Boolean vector of length twice the field degree of this
input, the matrix product small-bias seed is a vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, whose $i$th
coordinate is the output bit of the deterministic small-bias algorithm at coordinate
$i$, using the two seed components obtained from the Boolean vector.
\end{definition}

For every small-bias input and every Boolean seed string of length twice its chosen

two field elements obtained by splitting and decoding that string.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[One-third small-bias input]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput}
\label{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput}

Given a natural number $n>0$, define a small-bias input with output dimension $n$ and
bias numerator $1$ and denominator $3$. Thus its bias is positive and at most one half.
\end{definition}

input is $1/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scale for one-third bias]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput_scale}
\label{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput_scale}

\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $n$, the scale of the input with output dimension $n$ and
bias $1/3$ is $3n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Small-bias degree parameter]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasDegree}
\label{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasDegree}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, define the degree parameter to be the larger of $1$ and the
least natural number $k$ such that $2^k\ge 3n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Field degree for one-third bias]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput_fieldDegree}
\label{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput_fieldDegree}

\difficulty{3}
For every positive integer $n$, the field degree of the input with output dimension $n$
and bias $1/3$ equals $\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(3n)\rceil\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Matrix product random-bit count]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasRandomBits}

\label{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasRandomBits}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasDegree}
For each natural number $n$, define the matrix product small-bias random-bit count to be
the sum of the matrix product small-bias degree at $n$ with itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Small-bias logarithmic scale]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasLogScale}
\label{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasLogScale}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, define the logarithmic scale as the least natural number $k$
such that $2^k\ge n+1$, plus $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Small-bias degree bound]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasDegree_le}

For every natural number $n$, the matrix-product small-bias degree is at most
$2+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Random-bit count bound]

\lean{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasVerificationProgram}

membership-query learning program with Boolean output, formed by applying the seeded

one-third small-bias input of dimension $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[One-third bias verification guarantees]
\lean{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasVerificationAlgorithm_spec}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p153-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p166-b007
}
\label{FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasVerificationAlgorithm_spec}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.uniformPushforward, FABL.SmallBiasInput.epsilon, FABL.SmallBiasInput.fieldDegree, FABL.SmallBiasInput.fieldDegree_pos, FABL.boolSmallBiasSeedPairEquiv, FABL.deterministicSmallBiasAlgorithm, FABL.executableSmallBiasGenerator, FABL.executableSmallBiasOutputBitWork, FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput, FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasInput_epsilon, FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasRandomBits_eq, FABL.matrixProductOneThirdSmallBiasVerificationProgram, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasLogScale, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasRandomBits, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasRandomBits_isBigO, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasRandomBits_le, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasSeed, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasSeed_apply_spec, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasSeed_isBiased, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasVerification_complete, FABL.matrixProductSmallBiasVerification_sound, FABL.matrixProductVerificationCost, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_isBigO, FABL.matrixProductVerificationLocalWork_le, FABL.runWithCost_seededMatrixProductVerificationProgram, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationAcceptanceProbability, FABL.seededMatrixProductVerificationResult, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube $\{\pm1\}^n$
to $\{\pm1\}$, and let $A,B,C$ be $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb F_2$. Form the
input with output dimension $n$ and bias $1/3$, and run the associated seeded
verification algorithm against target $f$. Its output and cost have the law obtained by
choosing a uniform Boolean seed of length twice the input's field degree and returning
the verification result with cost $(0,0,r+6n^2+4n+1)$, where $r$ is that field degree.
The input bias is $1/3$, and the uniform pushforward of its seed map is small-bias with
this parameter; the seed length equals the specified random-bit count, which is at most
four times the specified logarithmic scale and is asymptotically $O$ of that scale. The
verifier's local work is at most $11(n+1)^2$ and is asymptotically $O((n+1)^2)$. For
every seed and coordinate $i$, the seed map agrees with the corresponding output of the
executable small-bias generator, and computing that output uses at most $16(i+1)(r+1)^2$
work. If $C=AB$, the acceptance probability is $1$; if $C\ne AB$, it is at most $2/3$.
\end{theorem}
